name: Fenris Industrial GroundHold L7 Labor Leg
product_name: Fenris Industrial GroundHold L7 Labor Leg
description:
The GroundHold L7 is a full bilateral leg replacement system engineered specifically to eliminate fatigue in workers who stand or move under load for extended shifts of up to 18 hours. The system uses a passive hydraulic load-distribution network that transfers vertical force from the spine across the entire foot chassis, reducing joint stress by an estimated 70% compared to biological legs under equivalent load. An embedded micro-stimulator array intermittently cycles minor proprioceptive signals to prevent the neural numbing associated with prolonged static posture, while the wide-base foot plate improves stability on uneven industrial flooring.

The L7 is standard equipment in GLMZ's manufacturing and logistics sectors, often provided by employers as part of a hire contract — which critics note creates dependency and indentured maintenance relationships. Workers call them Standpads, a name that captures both their utility and their unglamorous design.
installation_requirements: Full limb replacement, standard neural interface, can be performed at licensed medical clinic or employer-contracted installation facility
rejection_risk: Low — wide-profile osseointegration anchors distribute load well; rejection rare with standard immunosuppressant protocol
maintenance: Monthly hydraulic pressure check; micro-stimulator battery replacement every 90 days; annual full inspection recommended
side_effects: Users report emotional flatness after extended shifts due to proprioceptive suppression bleed into limbic feedback
Wide foot-plate creates gait awkwardness in non-industrial environments
Employer-locked maintenance contracts mean unauthorized repair voids neural interface warranty
Long-term users develop reduced sensitivity to physical fatigue cues, increasing risk of overwork injury in other body systems
cultural_context: GroundHold legs are the most common cyberlimb in the Gray Zone tier, and their wide flat foot is a class marker that polite society pretends not to notice. Labor advocacy groups have campaigned against employer-subsidized installation programs that create maintenance debt.
known_users: Factory floor and assembly line workers
Food service and hospitality workers on extended shifts
Tier 1-2 workers accepting employer hardware subsidies
story_hooks: A labor organizer has discovered that a major employer's L7 maintenance contracts contain a hidden clause allowing remote motor-function throttling during strikes
A the Gray Zone worker's GroundHold legs recorded and stored environmental sensor data from a restricted facility — data someone powerful wants erased
Fenris is quietly rolling out an L7 firmware update that extends maximum shift duration to 22 hours; someone needs to prove it before workers start collapsing
